Let me reconsider the maze structure. The player is at [14,14]-[18,18]. From the ASCII:

- Player at cols 14-19
- Col 20 is B (wall)
- Cols 21-25 are W (white path)
- Cols 26-30 are B (wall)
- Cols 31-35 are W (white path)
- Col 36 is B (wall)
- Col 37 is R (red)
- Col 38 is B (wall)
- Cols 39-50 are W
So the player is in a 6-wide room, and to the right is a wall. The player can't move RIGHT from here.
Let me think about what moves are possible from [14,14]-[18,18]:

- DOWN: would go to [20,14]-[24,18]
- LEFT: would go to [14,8]-[18,12] - but col 13 is the maze edge, so this would go outside the maze
- RIGHT: blocked (wall at col 20)
Let me check if DOWN works. From [14,14]-[18,18], DOWN would move to [20,14]-[24,18].
Row 19: `BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBWWWWWWWBRBWWWWWWWWW`
Cols 14-19 in the slice: positions 1-6 = BBBBBB (wall)
So DOWN would put the player on a wall. Let me try it anyway to see what happens.
Actually wait, let me reconsider. Maybe the player doesn't need to be on white cells. Maybe the player moves through the maze regardless of what's underneath, and the white cells are just visual decoration.
Let me try DOWN and see what happens.
